rationale_overall: Filtered out a large volume of non-investable noise this week: private-company items (SpaceX Falcon 9/Starship launches, OpenAI ad rollout, OpenAI 'Garlic' model, OpenAI debt financing), foreign/OTC names with no liquid US line (India's SDAL loitering-munition JV, Indian Navy warship handover, China's Long March-8A launch, CNOOC oilfield, Rosatom/Kudankulam fuel delivery, NPCIL waste story, ASX-listed Basin Energy, Canadian junior miners roundup), keyword false-matches (Rocket Doctor AI is a healthcare-AI shell, not a launch vehicle; 'Satellite High School' lockdown stories), generic/no-ticker market-research and prediction pieces (AI-in-healthcare TAM forecast, Fool.com 'next quantum stock' and 'AI stocks to buy' speculation, HHS AI strategy, AI safety report, robotics competition for middle-schoolers), and recurring geopolitical wire noise (Russia drone/missile barrages on Ukraine, China-Russia anti-missile drills) that names no tradable vehicle. Two items had real substance -- GE Vernova/TVA's $400M DOE grant for the first commercial SMR deployment, and a Cameco (CCJ) piece on nuclear-fuel strategic repositioning -- but both reinforce a nuclear-SMR wave already represented in the watchlist via SMR rather than clearing the bar for a swap: GEV is a large, already-run industrial name rather than an early-stage vehicle, and the Cameco piece is a narrative-framing opinion article, not a new contract or milestone. Nothing surfaced a rockets/robotics/quantum/demographics name with a genuine catalyst, and nothing argued a thesis breach in GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, or SMR. Holding the watchlist unchanged this week.
